paragraphs: Wayve's simulation team’s mission is to accelerate AV2.0 by incubating capabilities that become advantages, and generative world models and the synthetic data they produce are one of those. You sit between ML research and engineering, collaborating with scientists on architecture and conditioning, and with platform engineers on generation jobs, training artefacts, and how synthetic data is mixed into training. The role also requires strong Python and PyTorch, comfort with GPU training, debugging, and reading model code. This position will let me apply my experience in building pipelines and debugging implementations.

I satisfy the Python requirement through two key projects. First, I used scikit‑learn, TensorFlow and Keras to build end‑to‑end models that were served via FastAPI inside Docker containers, demonstrating research engineering and collaboration with data scientists. Second, I created a data pipeline in Python, also containerised with Docker, which processed fourteen source datasets and was managed through a controlled deployment workflow. Both efforts show my ability to deliver reliable Python code and to work closely with engineering teams. These implementations were reviewed and integrated into production environments, confirming their robustness and alignment with project goals.

I meet the PyTorch requirement with two relevant projects. In one, I built a model using PyTorch and packaged the training environment in Docker, ensuring reproducible builds and consistent execution across machines. In another, I containerised a PyTorch workflow, enabling other researchers to launch generation jobs on GPU clusters and to evaluate the impact of synthetic data on models. The containers incorporated version control, simplifying hand‑over to production. These experiences illustrate my competence with PyTorch and my ability to support experimentation in autonomous‑driving research.
